rows.text: Warsaw, 9 September 2026
Information from the meeting of the Monetary Policy Council held on 8-9 September 2026
The Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged:
reference rate at 3.75%;
lombard rate at 4.25%;
deposit rate at 3.25%;
rediscount rate at 3.80%;
discount rate at 3.85%.
In 2026 Q2, annual GDP growth rate accelerated in the euro area and slowed down in the United States.
Inflation in major advanced economies is higher than at the beginning of 2026, due to higher energy commodity prices.
The outlook for global activity and inflation is subject to uncertainty, stemming, in particular, from the conflict in the Middle East.

In Poland, according to the Statistics Poland preliminary estimate, the annual GDP growth in 2026 Q2 amounted to 3.9% (against 3.5% in 2026 Q1), amid an acceleration in investment growth and a slowdown in consumption growth.
In July 2026, retail sales and industrial output increased in annual terms, while construction and assembly production declined.
Annual wage growth in the national economy in 2026 Q2 decreased compared to the previous quarter.
This was accompanied by a fall in employment in the enterprise sector, which continued in July.
According to the Statistics Poland flash estimate, in August 2026 CPI inflation increased to 3.4% y/y (from 3.0% y/y in July).
This was mainly due to the rise in the annual growth in prices of fuels for personal transport equipment.
It can be estimated that in August inflation net of food and energy prices also increased.
Against this background the Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged.
Further decisions of the Council will depend on incoming information regarding prospects for inflation and economic activity in Poland.
Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context.
The shape of fiscal policy, changes in activity growth of the Polish economy and further developments in wage growth also remain risk factors for inflation outlook.

NBP will continue to take all necessary actions in order to ensure macroeconomic and financial stability, including above all to keep inflation at the level consistent with the NBP inflation target in the medium term.
NBP may intervene in the foreign exchange market.
